title: Tech Stack
text: This dashboard demonstrates how Quarto can serve as a multi-page dashboard framework, integrating multiple visualization technologies into a cohesive static site.

title: Tech Stack
text:
Architecture
The site is built as a Quarto website (type: website), not using the dashboard format. This provides:

Sidebar navigation with Bootstrap Icons
Full page layout with the Flatly theme
Table of contents per page
Static site output to _site/

title: Tech Stack
text:
Visualization Technologies

echarts4r (R)
Used on the Species Overview and Island Comparison pages.

What: R wrapper for Apache ECharts
Features: Boxplots, bar charts, scatter plots with tooltips
Pattern: Charts defined in R code blocks, rendered at build time
Data: palmerpenguins::penguins dataset loaded via setup.R
Extras: Toolbox with data zoom and save-as-image



Shinylive (R → WebAssembly)
Used on the Explorer page.

What: Shiny apps compiled to WebAssembly, running entirely in the browser
Features: Reactive UI with dropdowns and scatter plot
Pattern: Single {shinylive-r} code block with full UI + server
Extension: quarto-ext/shinylive
Layout: bslib::page_sidebar() for sidebar controls



React + D3 (JavaScript)
Used on the D3 Visualization page.

What: Custom interactive visualization built with React and D3
Features: Waffle chart with hover highlighting by species and island
Pattern: Separate Vite project in react-chart/, built to dist/, embedded via <iframe>
Key config: base: './' in vite.config.js for relative asset paths
Build: npm run build produces static files; Quarto copies dist/ to _site/

title: Tech Stack
text:
Data Tables
All data pages include reactable tables with:

Search functionality
Column filtering
Adjustable page sizes
Row highlighting

title: Tech Stack
text:
CSS
Custom stylesheet (styles.css) adapted with:

Penguin species color palette (orange/purple/green)
Gray scale design tokens
Inter font family
Styled panel tabsets, sidebar, tables, and iframes

title: Tech Stack
text:
How to Reproduce
# 1. Install the shinylive Quarto extension
quarto add quarto-ext/shinylive

# 2. Build the React chart
cd react-chart && npm install && npm run build && cd ..

# 3. Preview the site
quarto preview

# 4. Build the site
quarto render

title: D3 Visualization
text: This interactive waffle chart is built with React + D3 and embedded via an iframe. Each square represents one penguin, colored by species and grouped by island. Hover over species labels or island panels to highlight.

title: Palmer Penguins Dashboard
text:
Artwork by Allison Horst


This dashboard showcases how Quarto can integrate multiple visualization technologies into a cohesive, static-site dashboard.
No server required.
Each page showcases different technologies:

Species Overview — Boxplots of body measurements using {echarts4r} and page headers
Island Comparison — Scatter plots and composition charts using {echarts4r} and Quarto tabs
Explorer — Interactive app usign shinylive
D3 Visualization — Interactive waffle chart using React + D3
Data — Embedded data table using {reactable}

title: About
text:
The Palmer Penguins dataset contains measurements for 342 penguins from three species collected at three islands in the Palmer Archipelago, Antarctica.



Artwork by Allison Horst





Named for the thin black line running under their chin. Found exclusively on Dream Island.

Count: 68
Islands: Dream




The largest of the three species, with distinctive orange bills. Found primarily on Biscoe Island.

Count: 123
Islands: Biscoe




The most widespread species, found on all three islands. Characterized by shorter bills and moderate body mass.

Count: 151
Islands: Biscoe, Dream, Torgersen

title: About
text:
Measurements
The dataset includes four key body measurements:



Measurement
Description




Bill Length (mm)
Length of the penguin’s bill (culmen)


Bill Depth (mm)
Depth of the penguin’s bill


Flipper Length (mm)
Length of the penguin’s flipper


Body Mass (g)
Weight of the penguin






Artwork by Allison Horst

title: About
text:
Data Source
Data were collected by Dr. Kristen Gorman at Palmer Station, Antarctica, and made available through the palmerpenguins R package by Allison Horst.
